Server connections, Web hosts and the Web hosting panel

Manage the nginx and Apache virtual hosts of a Linux web server, the files of each document root and its TLS certificates (the private key never leaves the server), from one panel in Plugin Studio — over SSH to satom-webctl, a program that is the only thing SATOM's key can run on the server. The server never connects to SATOM, and both SATOM nodes drop any connection it tries to open.

👤 ForAdministratorAdvanced user
🔑 Permissionsstudio.script_library
📍 WherePlugin Studio → Connections → New → Server (a connection is /studio/connections/<id>); the apps come from Plugin Studio → Examples → Web hosts

What is it?#

💡Tip

Since 2026-11-06 the Web Server Manager in the Linux ADOM is the place to manage web servers (with your own SSH account and sudo). The Web hosts example apps below are switched off on upgrade; a server connection made here is a server there, and a server prepared with satom-webctl offers its agent key as the credential satom-webctl agent.

A Server connection points Plugin Studio at a Linux web server prepared with satom-webctl. Apps and scripts can then list the server's nginx and Apache virtual hosts, read and change their configuration, and browse, read, create, rename and delete the files of each document root.

❗Important

SATOM connects to the server; the server never connects to SATOM. The key SATOM uses opens no shell — the server runs satom-webctl and nothing else — and both SATOM nodes drop every new connection that comes from a managed server (hostguard). A script that goes wrong on the server, or whoever controls it, has no way into SATOM.

What does it do?#

  1. 1Plugin Studio app or scriptasks for one operation, e.g. files.list
  2. 2SATOMopens SSH as satom-mon, checks the pinned host key, sends one JSON request
  3. 3The web serversshd runs satom-webctl (forced command), confined to the document roots
  4. 4Ingestion gatethe answer is checked before SATOM uses it: size, strict JSON, closed schema
  5. 5The appshows the table, the file, the result
  • One program, a closed list of operations. On the server, SATOM's key is installed as restrict,command="/usr/local/bin/satom-webctl": no pty, no forwarding, no other command. satom-webctl reads one JSON request and answers one JSON object. Reads: info, vhosts.list, vhost.get, files.list, files.read. Writes: vhost.put, vhost.create, vhost.enable, vhost.disable, vhost.delete, files.write, files.mkdir, files.rename, files.delete.
  • No root on the server. satom-webctl runs as the unprivileged account satom-mon. It writes through ACLs on the managed roots and the site directories, and runs exactly two commands as root per web server, through sudoers: the configuration test and the reload.
  • A configuration change cannot leave the server broken. Every change is backed up, then tested with the server's own test (nginx -t, apachectl configtest). If the test fails, the previous file is restored and nothing is reloaded. A change that passes is applied with a reload, never a restart.
  • Files stay inside the document root. Paths are relative; .., absolute paths and symlinks that lead outside are refused. A virtual host whose document root is outside the roots given at install time (/var/www, /srv/www by default) is listed, but its files cannot be reached.
  • Every write keeps a backup on the server (/var/lib/satom-webctl/backups, the newest 200).

Safeguards on SATOM's side#

Safeguard What it means
Pinned host key A call is refused unless the server presents exactly the trusted host key. It is taken only by Fetch and trust on the connection page, never by a call. If the key changes, every call is refused and says so.
Ingestion gate Every answer is checked before use: size cap before parsing, strict JSON, one closed schema per operation (types, ranges, lengths, character sets). One bad value rejects the whole answer; the error names the field, never the value.
Writes are opt-in Allow writes on the connection (off by default). The server can refuse writes too (installer --read-only).
The key is SATOM's Generated by SATOM (Ed25519), kept in the vault or encrypted, never shown, never typed in.
Only from SATOM The installer command includes --from <SATOM nodes>: the key is accepted only from them.
Never packaged A server connection never travels in an app package.
hostguard Both SATOM nodes drop new connections coming from any managed server (nftables table inet satom_hostguard). SATOM's own nodes, the default gateway, the trusted proxies and the name servers are never blocked. Through a reverse proxy, the app itself answers 403 Forbidden to a managed server (the forwarded client address), before any other check.

Permissions#

🔑Permission

Creating and editing connections needs Plugin Studio (studio.script_library). Running the Web hosts apps follows each app's own access settings; a write also needs Allow writes on the connection.

How to use#

  1. Plugin Studio → Connections → New → Server. Enter the host (and the SSH port if it is not 22), then Generate key.
  2. Download satom-webctl, copy the archive to the server and, as root, run the installer command the page shows:

bash tar xzf satom-webctl.tar.gz && cd satom-webctl sudo bash install-satom-webctl.sh --pubkey 'ssh-ed25519 AAAA... satom-web01' \ --from {ip},{ip}

It creates satom-mon, installs satom-webctl, sets the ACLs and the two sudoers lines, and authorises the key. Options: --roots (default /var/www,/srv/www), --read-only, --uninstall [--purge]. 3. Fetch and trust the host key. Compare the fingerprint first with ssh-keygen -lf /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub on the server. 4. Test. It runs info and vhosts.list (both read-only). 5. Tick Allow writes when apps may change the server. 6. Plugin Studio → Examples → Web hosts → Install adds eighteen apps on the example connection ex-web-server. Point that connection at your server (steps 1–5) or change the apps' connection. Then publish the apps: a row button only opens a published app. 7. Open Plugins → Web hosts → Web hosting panel in the sidebar. They install under the menu group Web hosts, in the Linux ADOM when the console has one (a placeholder ADOM added in Settings → ADOMs; its sidebar draws Plugins below Dashboard) and in every ADOM otherwise. Each app's Settings tab changes both.

The Web hosting panel#

One page for the whole server, opened with the data already loaded (Refresh reads it again). Three tiles count the sites, the certificates and the certificates that need attention. Below them are three tabs:

  • Sites: every virtual host with Files, Configuration, Certificate (HTTPS sites), Enable/Disable and Delete.
  • Certificates: the ones that expire within 30 days and that a site serves come first, then all of them. Each row has View, Install (a request is waiting), Renew, Use on a site and Delete (only when no site uses it). A button appears only where it applies.
  • Server: the satom-webctl version, web servers, managed roots, read-only, the certificate folder and openssl.

New site and New certificate sit above the tabs. The panel only reads; every button opens the app that makes the change.

Certificates#

❗Important

The private key never leaves the server. Request or renew a certificate makes the key and its request (CSR) on the server. A Certificate Manager provider signs the request: the internal CA, or ACME (Let's Encrypt and others, DNS-01). The certificate goes back to the server. No operation returns a key, and Install refuses one.

  1. New certificate (or Renew on a row): name, common name, more names, key type (ec256 by default), and either sign and install with a provider or only make the request to sign it elsewhere.
  2. The certificate is installed and the sites that use it are tested and reloaded. If a test fails, the previous files come back.
  3. Use on a site points a site's certificate lines at it (backup, test, reload or restore).

A renewal keeps the sites on the old certificate until the new one is installed. The file paths do not change, so no site needs editing.

A certificate you already have (for example a wildcard): copy its key and chain by hand to /etc/satom-webctl/certs/<name>/privkey.pem (mode 0600, owner satom-mon) and fullchain.pem. The panel then lists, assigns and renews it.

Signing needs user_manage, the Certificate Manager's own permission. An app never widens who may issue certificates, and every signature is in the Audit Log (webhost.cert.sign).

Expiry. The scheduled action Web hosts — certificate expiry check (daily) is created by itself the first time a server's host key is trusted. It sends the administrators one bell notification per certificate at 30, 14 and 7 days left and when it expires, for the certificates an enabled site serves. A server it cannot read makes the run fail by name.

The Web hosts apps#

App What it does
Web hosting panel The whole server on one page (above).
Certificate What a certificate says, its certificate and chain, the request waiting — never the key.
Request or renew a certificate Key and request made on the server, signed by a provider, installed, sites reloaded.
Install a certificate The certificate issued for the server's request (refuses a key, another key's certificate, an expired one).
Use a certificate on a site / Delete a certificate Rewrite a site's certificate lines (tested, restored on failure) / delete an unused one (backup kept).
Web hosts The virtual hosts, with buttons per row: Files, Configuration, Enable/Disable, Delete — and New virtual host.
Virtual host configuration The configuration file; Edit opens the editor with the content and its hash.
Edit virtual host Saves it: backup, test, restore on failure, reload on success. A file changed by someone else since it was read is refused (conflict).
New virtual host From a template (static or PHP, optional HTTPS), inside a managed root; enabled, tested and reloaded — or removed again.
Enable or disable / Delete a virtual host Tested and reloaded; deleting keeps a backup and never touches the document root.
Files of a virtual host Browse a document root: Open, View, Rename, Delete per row; Up one folder, New file, New folder.
View a file / Edit or create a file Text files (binary files are sent as base64 and not shown).
Rename or move / Delete / New folder Inside the document root; deleting keeps a backup.

From a script#

A Script Library script that declares the connection calls it through the runner, which keeps the key outside the sandbox:

from satom_script import connection, result

web = connection("web01")
hosts = web.server("vhosts.list")["vhosts"]
page = web.server("files.read", server="nginx", name="shop", path="index.html", text=True)
result({"hosts": [h["name"] for h in hosts], "index": page.get("content")})
Advanced Details

hostguard, step by step. When a server connection is created, changed or deleted, SATOM writes the servers' addresses to data/hostguard/desired.json. satom-hostguard.path starts the privileged runner, which re-checks the list (never this node, the HA peer, the gateway, the trusted proxies or the name servers) and replaces the table inet satom_hostguard in one transaction. Only NEW connections are dropped: replies to the SSH sessions SATOM opens pass. The standby receives the file with the 5-minute data sync and applies the same rules. After a reboot, SATOM publishes the list again on start. What was applied is in /run/satom-hostguard.json on each node.

Troubleshooting#

"connection … has no trusted host key: press Fetch and trust on its page first"#

No host key is pinned yet, or it was forgotten (changing the host or the port forgets it). Press Fetch and trust after comparing the fingerprint.

"the host key of … changed … refused"#

The server presents another key: it was rebuilt, its key was replaced — or something else answers on that address. Check on the server, then fetch and trust the new key.

"… refused SATOM's key for satom-mon"#

The installer ran with another public key (for example, a new key was generated in SATOM afterwards). Run the installer again with the current key.

Every call takes about 25 seconds#

An unprivileged LXC container with systemd 252 or newer (Debian 12) without features: nesting=1: systemd-logind fails and every SSH login waits 25 s for it. Enable nesting on the container and restart it.

"… changes the server, and writes are off for connection …"#

Tick Allow writes on the connection. If the server answers read_only, the installer ran with --read-only.

"root_not_managed" / "outside_docroot"#

The document root is outside the roots given to the installer, or the path (or a symlink in it) leads outside the document root. Run the installer with --roots to add a root, or work inside the document root.

"the answer of … was refused by the ingestion gate"#

The server's answer did not match what that operation may return (a value with control characters, a field of the wrong type, an oversized answer). Nothing of it was used. The message carries a digest of the answer to match it with /var/log/satom-webctl/webctl.log on the server.
